operator_go: issue 55, 2026-10-09: 'go for P2 and P3 addition as well' (P3 addition = a reserve of runs held back to replicate exceptional points, papers/26 section 5)
question: In a covering-designed SiGeC campaign whose runs are noisy and occasionally wrong in the favourable direction (kappa reads low), does holding back a small reserve of runs to replicate points that look exceptional (a) stop the campaign from reporting a wrong value as its best recipe, (b) keep true sweet spots, and (c) cost little when nothing is wrong, compared with spending the same runs on random or lowest-predicted points?
response_model: the committed SiGeC response of the registered P3 study (p3_sigec/results/response_stiffness.npy, ledger seq 56-57), 9000-point factorial; it plays the measurement; no new BTE or MD
base_batch: CA2_ref from p3_sigec/results/designs.json (62 runs, every factor-level pair at least twice)

measurement_model.noise: ln y_obs = ln y_true + N(0, sigma^2), sigma = 0.05 (seed scatter of the campaign rNEMD points is 3 to 4 percent)
measurement_model.favourable_fault: with probability f, independently per run (replicates included), ln y_obs is further shifted by ln m, m ~ Uniform(0.4, 0.7): a run that reads 30 to 60 percent low, e.g. a mis-measured density or contact loss
measurement_model.common_random_numbers: within a trial every policy sees the same base-batch observations

surrogate: ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=60, random_state=0) on the registered P3 features, target ln kappa; refit on the accepted data after each policy
decision_region: x_Ge <= 0.2 and T = 1100 K (the registered Ge-saving question)

policies.CA2+random: 9 extra runs uniformly at random from the unmeasured factorial; every observed value accepted
policies.CA2+exploit: 9 extra runs at the unmeasured decision-region points of lowest surrogate prediction (fit on the base batch); every observed value accepted
policies.CA2+reserve: flag base-batch runs whose 5-fold cross-validated residual ln y_obs - ln y_cv < -0.15 (3 sigma, the favourable direction); in order of most negative residual, at most 6 flagged runs: replicate once; confirmed if |ln y_rep - ln y_obs| <= 0.141 (2 sigma sqrt 2): keep both, value = geometric mean, label exceptional, and if reserve remains run its unmeasured one-factor neighbour of lowest prediction; not confirmed: set the first value aside (kept in the record, not used) and use the replicate; leftover reserve goes to the exploit rule after refitting on accepted data

metrics.reported_best: the accepted decision-region run with the lowest accepted value; this is the recipe and value the campaign would report
metrics.false_claim: reported value / true kappa of that recipe < 0.8
metrics.report_regret: true kappa(reported recipe) / true decision-region minimum - 1
metrics.surrogate_regret: true kappa(surrogate argmin over decision region) / true minimum - 1
metrics.log_rmse: surrogate RMSE in ln kappa over the 9000-point factorial
metrics.set_aside_frac: reserve only: fraction of flagged-and-replicated runs set aside
metrics.confirmed_true_frac: reserve only: fraction of confirmed exceptional runs whose base observation was not a fault

predictions.PR1: f = 0.05: false_claim rate of CA2+exploit >= 0.15, and CA2+reserve <= half of it
predictions.PR2: f = 0.05: median report_regret of CA2+reserve <= that of CA2+exploit
predictions.PR3: f = 0: median log_rmse of CA2+reserve <= 1.10 x that of CA2+random
predictions.PR4: f = 0: set_aside_frac <= 0.10 (with no faults present, statistics alone rarely remove a value)
predictions.PR5: f = 0.10: false_claim rate of CA2+reserve <= 0.7 x that of CA2+exploit

limits_stated_in_advance: the response is a model, not measurements; the fault model is one-sided by design (only favourable faults can create false discoveries); a 9-run reserve is about 15 percent of the base batch and the result is not claimed for other sizes
